statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-6253: when curl uses different proxies for different URL schemes and follows a redirect that switches scheme, the credentials for the first proxy can be sent to the second proxy (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-6253.html). It affects curl 7.14.1 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/188c2f166a20fa97c2325b2da7d0e5cecc13725f, which resets the proxy credentials to those set in options when a redirect changes port or scheme, through a new Curl_reset_proxypwd() function. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI Alpine 3.23 main repository publishes curl builds 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the static libcurl.a shipped in curl-static, on x86_64 and aarch64, the object built from transfer.c defines Curl_reset_proxypwd() and Curl_reset_userpwd(), which the fix adds, in 8.20.0-r0 and 8.20.0-r1, and neither function exists in 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 or 8.19.0-r0. From 8.21.0-r0 on curl handles credentials through per-connection credential objects instead, and curl lists no release after 8.19.0 as affected. So 8.20.0-r0, the first build of curl 8.20.0, is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-6253: when curl uses different proxies for different URL schemes and follows a redirect that switches scheme, the credentials for the first proxy can be sent to the second proxy (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-6253.html). It affects curl 7.14.1 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/188c2f166a20fa97c2325b2da7d0e5cecc13725f, which resets the proxy credentials to those set in options when a redirect changes port or scheme, through a new Curl_reset_proxypwd() function. Debian backported the fix to trixie in 8.14.1-2+deb13u4 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6253). The DHI curl packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie curl 8.14.1-2; as of 2026-11-27 the DHI Debian repository publishes three of them (the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7) for amd64 and arm64, all later than 8.14.1-2+deb13u4, and each ships a Debian changelog that records the fix under 8.14.1-2+deb13u4. In the debug information of libcurl4t64 and libcurl3t64-gnutls of all three builds, on amd64 and arm64, libcurl defines Curl_reset_proxypwd() and Curl_reset_userpwd(), the functions the fix adds, which Debian's own unfixed 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 libcurl4t64 build (amd64) does not define. Every published build carries the fix, so the fixed version is the lowest published one, the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5.
